statements.quote: Net cash flows from investing activities and their variability across each period related primarily to capital expenditures, which were $11.34 billion and $8.90 billion for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, mainly for AI-related capital expenditures, global factory expansion and machinery and equipment as we expand and enhance our product roadmap.
statements.notes: Total capex with AI-related capex named first among drivers; the AI portion itself is not stated. The $8.90 billion figure is for 2023, the prior year, and is not recorded.

statements.quote: Owing and subject to the foregoing as well as the pipeline of announced projects under development, all other continuing infrastructure growth and varying levels of inflation, we currently expect our capital expenditures to exceed $11.00 billion in 2025 and in each of the following two fiscal years.
statements.notes: "Exceed $11.00 billion" is a floor with no upper bound. The figure is recorded as both low and high. The sentence ties the total to AI only through "the foregoing", meaning the previous sentence, which lists investing in autonomy and other AI-enabled training and products among the capex projects. That is why confidence is lower. The same outlook also covers "each of the following two fiscal years", which the sentence does not name, so no statements are recorded for those years.

statements.quote: The overall increases were primarily driven by additional costs year over year related to AI programs.
statements.notes: This refers to the $571 million (14%) increase in R&D expense in 2024 stated in the previous sentence. The AI-related share of that increase is not quantified, so it is recorded as qualitative. The sentence names no year, so code will apply the reported year 2024.
